questions.question: Real $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ are called similar if $B=P^{-1}AP$ for some $n\times n$ matrix $P$. Which condition on $P$ does the definition require?
options: $P$ must be invertible, so that $P^{-1}$ exists
$P$ must be diagonal, so that it only rescales

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix and $B=P^{-1}AP$ for an invertible $P$. Which of the following generally differs between $A$ and $B$?
Suppose $B=P^{-1}AP$ for an invertible matrix $P$. Which expression recovers $A$ from $B$?
Let $A$ be a real $n\times n$ matrix and $E$ an invertible $n\times n$ matrix, for instance a product of elementary row operations. How is the one-sided product $EA$ related to $A$?
options: It is similar to $A$, since $E$ is invertible
It has the eigenvalues of $A$, but other eigenvectors
It is row equivalent to $A$, but its eigenvalues can differ
It is similar to $A$ whenever $E$ is diagonal

questions.question: In $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $A$ be the matrix of a linear operator in standard coordinates, and let the columns of an invertible matrix $P$ form a basis $\mathcal{B}$. What does $P^{-1}AP$ represent?
options: A new operator: $A$ followed by a change of basis
The standard matrix of the operator applied to the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$
The matrix converting $\mathcal{B}$-coordinates into standard ones

questions.question: The matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ satisfies $A(1,1)^{\top}=3(1,1)^{\top}$. Let $B=P^{-1}AP$ with $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. Which vector is an eigenvector of $B$ for the eigenvalue $3$?
The matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\1&4\end{pmatrix}$ has trace $7$ and determinant $10$. Which diagonal matrix is similar to $A$?
Let $A=PDP^{-1}$ with $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $D=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$, so that $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. What is $A^3$?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$. Compute the similar matrix $P^{-1}AP$.

The matrices $M_1=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $M_2=2I_2$ have the same characteristic polynomial $(\lambda-2)^2$. Which quantity, unchanged under similarity, shows that they are not similar?
Suppose $B=P^{-1}AP$ and $C=Q^{-1}BQ$ for invertible matrices $P$ and $Q$. Which matrix $R$ gives $C=R^{-1}AR$?

A real symmetric matrix $A$ satisfies $Q^{\top}AQ=\Lambda$, where $\Lambda$ is diagonal and the columns of $Q$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$. Why is $A\mapsto Q^{\top}AQ$ a similarity transformation?
options: Transpose and inverse coincide here because $\Lambda$ is diagonal

questions.question: A real $n\times n$ matrix $A$ satisfies $A^2-5A+6I=O$, and $B=P^{-1}AP$ for an invertible $P$. Does $B$ satisfy the same equation?
options: Only if $P$ commutes with $A$, so that $B=A$

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&5&7\\0&2&4\\0&0&3\end{pmatrix}$ and let $B=P^{-1}AP$ for some invertible $3\times3$ matrix $P$. What is $\det(B+I)$?
options: It depends on the choice of $P$

questions.question: Let $A=PDP^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ with $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $D=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Using $\mathrm{e}^{At}=P \mathrm{e}^{Dt}P^{-1}$, what is the matrix exponential $\mathrm{e}^{At}$?
Which of the following real $2\times2$ matrices is similar to a diagonal matrix, that is, equals $PDP^{-1}$ for some invertible $P$ and diagonal $D$?
Two real $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ have the same characteristic polynomial. Which extra assumption guarantees that $A$ and $B$ are similar?
options: Both have the same trace and determinant

questions.question: Let $A$ be a real symmetric $n\times n$ matrix and $B=P^{-1}AP$ for an invertible, not necessarily orthogonal, matrix $P$. Which property must $B$ have?
options: Symmetry, since similarity preserves every property of $A$
The eigenvalues of $A$; $B$ need not be symmetric
The eigenvectors of $A$, together with its eigenvalues
A diagonal form, since a symmetric $A$ is diagonalizable

questions.question: For a real parameter $a$, let $M_a=\begin{pmatrix}2&a\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $J=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$. For which values of $a$ is $M_a$ similar to $J$?
The matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}5&-1\\6&0\end{pmatrix}$ has eigenvalues $3$ and $2$. Which invertible matrix $P$ satisfies $P^{-1}AP=\operatorname{diag}(3,2)$?
